transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-14
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ryan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alice Chen (ZenMed CTO), Bob Martinez (ZenMed Head of Security), Daniel Park (ZenMed Infra)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Security posture discussion focused on SOC2/ISO, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, audit logs, KMS/BYOK, data retention and residency.
- ZenMed is healthcare-focused, PHI concerns, leaning toward Dedicated or Private deployment but evaluating Hosted with strong controls.
- Next steps: share SOC2 report, SAML metadata, schedule technical deep dive and confirm retention windows.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Ryan: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm ryan from Redwood, i'll kick us off.
[00:00:06] Alice: Hi yeah thanks, i'm alice, CTO at zenmed. we've got bob and daniel here.
[00:00:12] Bob: Hey all.
[00:00:16] Ryan: Quick agenda, security posture review, what controls you need, how redwood supports hosted/dedicated/private, then open q and next steps. sound good?
[00:00:24] Alice: Yep good.
[00:00:30] Priya: hi folks, priya here. i'll jump into the technical bits around encryption, keys, and audit logs later.
[00:00:36] Bob: To set context, we handle PHI so we have strict requirements on data residency, KMS, and auditability. we're exploring hosted because of speed but privacy and compliance are big factors.
[00:00:47] Ryan: totally, makes sense. maybe start with SOC2/ISO. we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications; i can share the attestation and the summary controls.
[00:00:58] Alice: is that public? will you send the full report or a redacted artifact?
[00:01:03] Ryan: we typically send the SOC2 report under an NDA; the summary and controls matrix we can share publicly. i'll put links in the follow-up.
[00:01:12] Bob: perfect. a couple questions on hosted: do you allow encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys? we need BYOK/HSM for some workflows.
[00:01:22] Priya: yes, we support customer-managed keys, BYOK, and HSM integration. for hosted we offer KMS integration and key rotation policies; in some enterprise plans you can bring keys through our KMS connector or use a dedicated HSM.
[00:01:36] Alice: any constraints with BYOK and model caching or kv cache? like does BYOK impact ability to use prefix cache?
[00:01:44] Priya: good q - caching is orthogonal, but when keys are customer-managed we encrypt the cached artifacts with a service key wrapped by customer KMS; there are perf tradeoffs but we've optimized for it. i can share notes; sometimes there is slightly higher latency on first token as bindings occur.
[00:01:58] Daniel: yep that latency note matters for us, our SLAs are tight for real-time triage flows. what are typical numbers?
[00:02:06] Priya: on hosted with BYOK we see micro-to-single-digit ms overhead on token serving, but first request can be 50-150ms depending on key exchange. with dedicated pools it's negligible.
[00:02:19] Bob: we also need audit logs that are tamper-evident and exportable to our SIEM, splunk. retention configurable to 7 years for some audit trails.
[00:02:28] Ryan: we stream audit logs to customer endpoints via secure syslog or S3 with encryption; we also support integration with major SIEMs. retention windows are configurable depending on plan; for private deployments you control retention fully.
[00:02:43] Alice: do you provide immutable/audit-proof logs or do customers need to ship to their own WORM store?
[00:02:50] Priya: we provide append-only logs with cryptographic checksums on our side, but for regulatory-grade WORM-style retention we recommend exporting to customer's write-once storage - we can automate exports.
[00:03:03] Bob: good. about SSO - we use Okta. we need SAML and SCIM provisioning, plus role mapping to enforce RBAC.
[00:03:12] Ryan: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; you can map Okta groups to roles in our console. we also have SCIM SCIM? [laughs] sometimes the transcript will repeat, but yes SCIM provisioning is supported.
[00:03:25] Priya: for RBAC we have predefined roles (admin, dev, read-only) and custom roles for resource scoping. you can restrict who can create deployments, view logs, or export data.
[00:03:37] Daniel: can RBAC be scoped by project or VPC? we want infra teams to have network-level access but not see app-level data.
[00:03:44] Priya: yes, roles are scoped by project and environment. you can create org-level roles and project roles; network configs are treated as infra resources and can be restricted.
[00:03:55] Bob: data residency - we need EU-only and US-only processing for some customers. hosted has regions?
[00:04:02] Ryan: hosted operates in multiple regions; customers can pin their traffic to regions. for strict residency often customers choose dedicated or private so data never leaves a VPC/region.
[00:04:13] Alice: what's the difference operationally between dedicated and private? liability and isolation wise?
[00:04:18] Priya: dedicated is a reserved GPU pool in our infra with tenant isolation - network isolation and dedicated capacity, but the control plane runs in our cloud. private is customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem) where the customer owns networking and we provide operator tooling - more options for air-gapped or regulated workloads.
[00:04:34] Alice: and for private, do we still get updates and security patches from Redwood?
[00:04:38] Ryan: yes we ship signed updates; the upgrade cadence is agreed in the contract, and you can test upgrades in a staging instance.
[00:04:45] Daniel: what about pen tests and vuln disclosure - do you share results?
[00:04:49] Priya: we run annual pentests and external vuln scans; we share redacted reports with customers under NDA and have a responsible disclosure program.
[00:04:58] Bob: encryption in transit - TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS support?
[00:05:03] Priya: TLS 1.2+ by default, and mTLS is supported for private and dedicated endpoints; hosted can support mTLS on enterprise plans.
[00:05:12] Alice: logging details - do logs include prompt text? we need to mask PHI.
[00:05:18] Ryan: by default we log metadata and token counts; you can configure whether full prompts are logged. for PHI workloads we recommend disabling full prompt persistence and enabling on-the-fly redaction or client-side redaction.
[00:05:33] Bob: and are you able to do client-side encryption such that PII never hits your plaintext memory?
[00:05:38] Priya: complete client-side homomorphic encryption isn't supported; but we support tokenization/encryption at the application layer and partial encryption patterns, plus proxying through private deployments so plaintext never leaves the customer's network.
[00:05:53] Daniel: any limitations on model features in private? like streaming, function calling, tool calling?
[00:06:00] Priya: feature parity is close; streaming and function calling are supported in private and dedicated, though certain integrations (managed telemetry) are optional.
[00:06:09] Alice: compliance attestations - you mentioned SOC2 and ISO. any HIPAA-specific work?
[00:06:15] Ryan: we provide a HIPAA addendum for private/dedicated customers; for hosted we have customers under a BAA on certain plans - we'd need to scope the data flows.
[00:06:26] Bob: can you walk through typical network topology for private deployment? VPN, peering, or direct connect?
[00:06:33] Priya: typical options: VPC peering, AWS Direct Connect, private link, or on-prem with a VPN. we provide an ops runbook with firewall rules, whitelisting, and port lists. i'll attach the runbook.
[00:06:48] Daniel: any special ports for GPU nodes?
[00:06:52] Priya: mainly standard HTTPS, a few internal control ports - non-internet facing. we'll include exact port numbers in the runbook.
[00:06:59] Ryan: timeline wise, are you targeting a POC and then pilot? what's your procurement window?
[00:07:06] Alice: we'd like a 30-day POC to test latency and audit exports, then pilot in q3, budget approved but security sign-off is gating.
[00:07:14] Bob: i'll need to validate key rotation policies and proof of log integrity before sign-off.
[00:07:20] Ryan: understood. for the POC we can provide a scoped dedicated environment or a private eval depending on preference. which would you prefer?
[00:07:28] Alice: start with dedicated reserved pool, simpler to spin up, then private if gating remains.
[00:07:35] Priya: ok we'll draft a POC plan for dedicated with BYOK and audit log streaming to ZenMed test account.
[00:07:42] Daniel: about costs - dedicated vs hosted how different for your unit economics?
[00:07:48] Ryan: dedicated has a commit/seat model with lower per-token variable cost and more predictable latency; hosted is usage-based and more elastic but could be higher variable cost. we'll send a pricing sketch.
[00:07:59] Alice: one more operational question - who has access to debug traces in production?
[00:08:05] Priya: access to debug/traces is RBAC controlled; by default only Redwood SREs and designated customer admins can see traces; we also have an access review and can provide time-bound access with audit trail.
[00:08:18] Bob: do you support embargoed access to trace data for audits?
[00:08:22] Ryan: yes we can provide time-limited access and export snapshots under NDA.
[00:08:30] Alice: ok good.
[00:08:35] Bob: encryption key rotation frequency?
[00:08:38] Priya: we support automatic rotation policies; customers can set rotation cadence, and we support on-demand rotations. key rotation will tie into the KMS provider's policies.
[00:08:47] Daniel: what about multi-tenancy data leakage risk during memory reuse on GPU?
[00:08:53] Priya: we have memory isolation and scrubbing between sessions; for high-assurance we recommend dedicated or private pools to eliminate cross-tenant memory reuse risk.
[00:09:04] Alice: any third-party subprocesses that could exfiltrate data? 3rd-party libs?
[00:09:09] Priya: we maintain a vetted software bill of materials (SBOM) and run SCA scans; we can share SBOM under NDA.
[00:09:17] Bob: excellent. how do you handle backups and restore for model artifacts and customer config?
[00:09:22] Ryan: backups are encrypted and versioned; for private deployments backups can be to customer-owned storage. restore procedures are documented.
[00:09:32] Alice: what about retention for prompts vs logs? can we set separate retention policies?
[00:09:37] Priya: yes, prompts, embeddings, and audit logs have separate retention policies you can configure per-project.
[00:09:45] Daniel: is there a way to auto-redact or obfuscate PHI in logs before they leave the customer environment?
[00:09:52] Priya: we have a redaction hook that can run as a preprocessor; in private deployments you can run it inside your network so PHI never leaves. hosted supports it as a managed option as well.
[00:10:03] Bob: ok let's recap next steps.
[00:10:05] Ryan: i'll send SOC2/ISO docs and security whitepaper, priya will send SAML/SCIM guide and runbook, we'll schedule a technical deep dive and POC plan for dedicated.
[00:10:15] Alice: that works. thanks everyone.
[00:10:18] Ryan: thanks all.

[00:10:20] Note: transcript ends; recording continued but auto-trimmed in export.
